sections.overview: The Common Buttonquail is a small ground-dwelling bird with a broad Old World range from Africa through Asia, historically reaching Iberia.
sections.identification: It is a small, compact buttonquail; females are more brightly marked than males.
sections.habitat: Across its range it uses dry sandy ground with low scrub or grass cover. The Mediterranean form occupied coastal scrub and dry grassland.
sections.diet: It is omnivorous, taking insects, snails and worms as well as shoots and seeds.
sections.behavior: It is exceptionally secretive and keeps to ground cover, where its earthy plumage is hard to see.
sections.reproduction: The species is polyandrous: a female may mate with several males, and males incubate the eggs and care for the chicks.
sections.ecology: Turnix sylvaticus includes several subspecies; SEO/BirdLife’s account specifically describes the nominate Mediterranean form found in Spain.
sections.conservation: SEO/BirdLife reports the Andalusian form regionally extinct in Europe and a remaining population in Morocco; that regional account is not a global status statement.
